findings.source_passage: Now this ambergris is a very curious substance, and so important as an article of commerce, that in 1791 a certain Nantucket-born Captain Coffin was examined at the bar of the English House of Commons on that subject.
findings.why_it_matters: The Captain Coffin anecdote—examined at the bar of the English House of Commons—is a voice-establishing, Melvillean digressive opener that sets the mock-scholarly register of the entire chapter. Its absence strips the chapter of its characteristic introductory tone.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the Captain Coffin sentence as the chapter's opening, verbatim or near-verbatim; it is the tonal key of the passage.

findings.source_passage: I should like to conclude the chapter with the above appeal, but cannot, owing to my anxiety to repel a charge often made against whalemen
findings.source_locator: Paragraph beginning 'I should like to conclude'
findings.why_it_matters: This self-conscious metanarrative aside—Ishmael announcing he would like to stop but cannot—is a signature instance of voice-driven ironic digression. Its erasure collapses the narrator's presence and the rhetorical drama of the chapter's two-part structure.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the self-reflexive transition sentence ('I should like to conclude the chapter … but cannot') to preserve the narrator's ironic voice and the structural commentary.

findings.source_passage: the learned Fogo Von Slack, in his great work on Smells, a text-book on that subject
findings.why_it_matters: The invented authority 'Fogo Von Slack' and his 'great work on Smells' is a characteristic Melvillean satirical joke—mock-scholarly citation—that defines the chapter's comic register. Its suppression flattens the irony.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the reference to 'the learned Fogo Von Slack, in his great work on Smells, a text-book on that subject'; it is brief and tonally essential.

findings.source_passage: nor can the whale possibly be otherwise than fragrant, when, as a general thing, he enjoys such high health; taking abundance of exercise; always out of doors; though, it is true, seldom in the open air.
findings.source_locator: Final paragraph, before the whale's flukes simile
findings.why_it_matters: The witty paradox ('always out of doors; though, it is true, seldom in the open air') is a characteristically Melvillean joke that the draft drops entirely, slightly reducing the playfulness that precedes the climactic elephant simile.
findings.suggested_fix: Insert the clause before the flukes simile to preserve the wit and tonal build toward the chapter's close.

summary: Three medium-severity findings—erasure of the Captain Coffin opening, the self-reflexive 'I should like to conclude' metanarrative aside, and the mock-scholarly 'Fogo Von Slack' satirical citation—collectively constitute a pattern of voice erasure that triggers regeneration.
